subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a militarized cyberpunk truck design—six wheels, a turret, armor plates, and neon glow details—and considering whether it needs wheel joints or can stay as a simpler static structure like other props.

I'm sketching the skeleton with a root chassis joint and separate joints for wheels, turret, and gun, then setting the truck's overall dimensions at roughly 8m long, 2.8m wide, and 3.2m tall with the cab facing forward. I'm also picking a gunmetal and olive-black palette with neon cyan, magenta, and orange accents, pulling in metal and panelled materials from the clockwork kit, and planning several SVG textures like hazard stripes, door numbers, and HUD screens to add detail.

Now I'm working out wheel placement across three axles with radius 0.62 tires, plus chassis rails, crossmembers, axle cylinders with differential spheres, and a per-wheel breakdown of tire, rim, and tread geometry.

Each wheel gets a tire, hub cap with glowing ring, lug nuts, and a merged tread block ring of 12 boxes to keep part count efficient. Then I'm defining wheel joints attached to the chassis at the correct x/y/z offsets to hang all these parts.

Now I'm working out the cab design -- a tall, low-poly angular shape built by extruding a side profile polygon (in the z-y plane) to give it width, starting with the hood slope and roofline points.

Adding a slim tilted windshield as a thin dark box angled backward to match the slope between the hood and roofline, with a dark teal glass tint.

Defining window outline geometry...

For the front end, I'm sketching hood vents with glowing orange strips, a massive ram bumper block positioned forward, and possibly a plow wedge, with hazard stripe texturing on the bumper.

Up top I'm adding slim glowing headlight bars plus round lamps, a roof light bar in magenta/amber, and a sensor array with a radar dish, antenna rods with glowing red tips, and small sensor boxes. I'm planning a turret mount centered on the rear cargo area for twin railguns, and sketching the cargo bed as an armored container module with a lower hull box section.

Now I'm working out the hull geometry more precisely, extruding a panelled profile from the rear to front with slanted top plates, adding a turret and missile pod rack at the back, plus angled side armor skirts over the wheels. I'm figuring out the exact z-coordinates for the hull length and wheel placement relative to the body width.

Still adjusting proportions so wheels sit outside the hull without clipping -- narrowing the hull thickness, shifting wheel centers outward, and sizing the angled fenders to sit over each wheel.

I'm adding armored fender slabs and a partial side skirt plate that hangs over the upper half of the wheels like a mudguard, then starting the cab geometry sized to sit flush against the hull's front edge.

Next I'm fine-tuning the hull-to-cab overlap so the cab's rear-top bump sits just above the hull, then working out axle positions for the front and tandem rear wheels, settling on a wheelbase with the front axle forward and the two rear axles bunched closer together.

I'm also checking that the chassis rails, belly plate, and wheel radii keep the bottom of the vehicle at ground level, then sizing the overall height and length so the cab roof plus antenna stays near 4 meters and the hull spans about 8.8 meters. Now I'm sketching the turret as a lathed ring base with an extruded angular body sitting on the hull.

Next I'm setting up the turret and gun joints, positioning the gun pivot forward on the turret for a twin-barrel railgun look, with each barrel built from rods, glowing emitter rings, and a muzzle brake box. Writing barrel geometry...

I need the barrel height to clear the cab roof without making the whole vehicle too tall, so I'll pull the turret back to z -1.6 with a shorter barrel length ending around z 1.5-1.6, keeping the barrel at y 3.1 to avoid clashing with the roof at y 3.2.

For the rear missile pods, I'm placing two tilted box pods near the hull sides at x ±0.6, z -3.0, angled upward-back around 30 degrees, textured with a 3x2 tube pattern on the front face, though the texture will likely show on all faces of the box.

Working out the rotation math confirms θ=-35° tilts the pod axis upward-forward correctly, matching the windshield normal calculation. Now I'm thinking through cab details: pillar framing, mirror-camera stalks with glow, and a door emblem decal placed on the side face.

For the emblem I'm avoiding real brand names, designing a fictional "NOMAD-77" hex-shield insignia with hazard stripes instead, plus cyan/magenta neon strips running vertically along the hull. I'm also planning a textured side panel with circuit/camo patterns and stylized sans-serif text to give the hull a cyberpunk feel.

Now I'm working out the plane orientation math for the panel so the artwork reads correctly from outside the hull on both the +x and -x sides, accounting for how the aim direction and up vector determine which local axis maps to width.

Good, the decal orientation checks out on both sides, so the readability is fine regardless of which side it faces. Now I'm adding the cab details — a hazard-striped bumper texture, a front plow-style bumper with an angular splitter, bull-bar uprights, and the grille.

Adding grille and headlights...

Grille width settles at 1.4 between ±0.7. Now planning the roof details: a light bar up front glowing orange/magenta, thin antenna rods at the rear corners with red tips, and a radar dish built as a lathed concave profile tilted on the roof.

Next I'm positioning exhaust stacks behind the cab on the hull's front corners, checking their placement against the fenders to avoid clashes, and adding heat shield boxes plus top deck plating details to the hull.

Then I'm detailing the rear with a ramp door texture, slanted rear profile, glowing red tail light strips, hazard decals, a tow hitch, and a rear bumper box. For the sides, I'm adding stowage lockers and strapped drum cylinders between the wheel wells.

Underneath, I'm placing the chassis, driveshaft, differential, and cylindrical fuel tanks mounted between the axles, checking that their positioning along the z-axis avoids clashing with the front and mid wheel wells, then adding neon underglow strips for a cyberpunk touch.

For the top deck, I'm sketching out armored cargo crates, a rolled cable, a comms antenna array, and a glowing hexagonal reactor core with a ring near the rear, deciding to skip the holo-projection and drone pods to keep complexity manageable.

Now I'm defining the hull material itself: a dark gunmetal teal mottled base with countershading for depth, then overlaying a panelled texture with fine seams and small rivets, keeping texel density reasonable for the truck's large scale.

Checking resolution math, I bump the paint size to 2048 so seams stay visible without excessive aliasing, and consider enlarging panel size as a backup. For the color scheme, I'm settling on a matte dark blue-grey hull with orange, cyan, and magenta accent stripes for contrast.

I'm sketching the builder setup: a root chassis joint, a helper box function for parts, and wheel joints, while keeping the flat color palette under 64 entries to stay efficient.

To avoid type issues I'll derive the joint type from the builder's own joint method rather than importing it separately, and use conditional spreads so optional rotation and texture props don't break things when undefined. I'm also planning mirror and glow helper wrappers, noting glow needs a standard material rather than flat paint colors.

For the tire tread geometry, I'm working out how to build the repeated block pattern around the wheel circumference in the wheel's local space—placing boxes at angles around a circle, rotating each to face outward, then translating into position—so it can later be oriented along the correct wheel axis in the full model.

Now I'm defining a wheel-building function that creates joints attached to the chassis at the correct x/z positions with hinge orientation along the x-axis, naming each wheel joint (wheelL1, wheelR1, etc.) and setting up the cylinder geometry for the tyres.

Adding lug nuts next: six small cylinders arranged in a circle at radius .17 around the hub, merged together, with the tire colored dark charcoal and the rim given a metallic steel paint with slight tarnish.

Now I'm adding axle rods spanning across the chassis, a differential sphere at the center, and considering coil springs and shock absorbers near the wheel mounts, building vertical coils from the axle up to the chassis using a sweep along a helical path.

Still defining the hull...

Now I'm positioning the turret and cab above the hull top, setting barrel and roofline heights, then sketching the cab outline with its hood, windshield, and roof points.

I'm working out the windshield geometry—its center, length, and slope angle—so the glass panel sits flush against the cab's sloped surface with a slight outward offset, and I'm placing the dark A-pillar frames alongside it.

Now I'm adding armor plates and window glass to the cab sides: door panels with hull-colored plating and accent trim lines, plus the side window glass positioned just outboard of the armor, running from roughly waist height up to the roofline.

I'm also planning door emblem decals and hull side panels positioned between the front and rear wheel wells, sitting above the fender tops with enough clearance to avoid overlapping the armor plating.

For the fenders, I'm designing a slab plus outer lip per wheel, positioning them to clear the tire tops and sit flush with the tire's outer edge, plus adding mud flaps trailing behind each wheel for detail.

Now I'm figuring out the underglow neon strips along the hull's bottom edge, checking they clear the fender geometry at the overlap zones so the magenta glow reads cleanly beneath the chassis.

I'm also laying out the cab and hull side stripes in cyan and magenta, then turning to the top deck details—placing a hexagonal reactor cylinder with a cyan glow near the rear and positioning side pods so they don't crowd the reactor's center position.

Working out pod box dimensions and tilt angle...

I'm sketching the pod body as a dark box with rounded circular details and an orange tip, then working out how it sits tilted on the deck with supporting cradle boxes underneath to match the slope where the hull curves down toward the rear.

Now I'm shifting to the turret, computing its rotated outline points to extrude a profile shape with the right thickness and taper along the z-axis.

Still placing turret geometry...

Placing more components on turret and cab roof: a light bar, radar mast, and a tilted radar dish, all positioned relative to the roof plane and barrel height so nothing collides with existing parts.

I'm shifting the radar dish and lidar dome outward in x to avoid overlapping the barrels, then considering adding small crates on the top deck between the turret and cab, adjusting their position relative to the radar placement.

Now I'm placing antenna whips at the rear corners with glowing red tips, then working out the rear lights, hazard plate with markings, and bumper geometry near the sloped tail section.

I'm now working out the front bumper dimensions and position, adding an armor-colored hazard stripe plane on the front face, and adjusting how it protrudes relative to the cab front.

For the plow, I'm adding small forward-pointing cone spikes at the bumper corners and a row of tooth-like cones along the bottom, plus a glowing grille plane and boxy headlight shapes positioned symmetrically on either side of center.

Now I'm figuring out the hood details: small orange-glowing vent slits placed along a sloped hood surface, with a helper function to compute the hood's y-position based on its tilt angle, plus side marker lights as tiny orange boxes along the cab.

Placing mirror boxes at the cab corners with stalks and glowing cyan camera faces, then adding side exhaust stacks near the cab with cylinder bodies, brackets, and glowing orange cap rings, while checking they don't collide with the cab's width.

Now I'm checking the stack placement clears the hull geometry, adding heat-shield clamp rings, and skipping extras like fuel tanks and driveshafts. I'm considering top hull details like deck ribs, vent grates with subtle orange glow, and edge trim rails along the sides.

I'm also working out side armor details — rivet-lined vertical ribs positioned at panel segment boundaries along the hull sides, making sure they align with the decal panels rather than overlapping awkwardly, plus a rear hatch plate for the sloped hull back.

I'm designing the texture content for each panel segment: four cells covering a "07" marking, hazard stripes, grid vents, and directional arrows, sized to match the panel dimensions. I'm skipping extras like side ladders, drone launchers, and roof turret cameras to keep things simpler, just adding the antenna array on the roof instead, and double-checking fender clearance against the panel height.

Now I'm laying out the full texture list I'll need: hazard stripes, side panel cells, door emblem, grille, front pod, windshield glass with HUD reflections, rear plate, and a small side window reuse of the glass texture, roughly eight total. I'm making sure strokes are thick enough to read at small sizes, and for the hazard texture I'm generating a rotated diagonal yellow-and-black pattern with a border to render as the alternating stripe effect.

For the side decal I'm sketching a 520x100 panel divided into cells with a dark fill and contrasting stroke: a bold orange "07" unit number in one cell, small hazard-and-cyan-line accents in another, horizontal vent slits with a cyan glow in a third, and magenta chevrons with "2077" text in the last, mixing monospace and sans-serif fonts for contrast. For the door emblem I'm drawing a hexagonal shield with a dark fill and orange outline, containing a stylized wolf-eye motif—a cyan ring with a vertical slit pupil—plus "N-77" lettering.

Now I'm detailing the grille (dark rounded rect with six cyan horizontal slits and a diamond emblem), the engine pod (a 3x2 grid of dark circles with orange rims and red-orange inner cores suggesting nose cones), the canopy glass (a cyan-to-dark gradient with faint diagonal light streaks and a tiny "TGT LOCK" HUD readout), and the rear panel (dark background with orange "NOMAD-77" text, a hazard stripe, a barcode, and a "2077-NX" plate).

I'm also working out a merge helper that combines groups of boxes and cones into single geometries, rotating and positioning each piece before merging them so they can be painted with consistent colors and bone attachments, while making sure all the geometries share matching vertex attributes for a clean merge.

Fixing the vector spread issue by indexing array elements directly instead, and defining a P3 tuple type for 3D points to keep things type-safe.

Rotation uses an XYZ degree tuple, and I need to import coil, metal, panelled, and INK from the clockwork kit along with glow from the glow kit. For joints, each wheel needs a parent reference like chassis to avoid the root-joint error, and I'm considering whether to assign a "spine" role to the chassis.

I'm skipping extra wheel roles and setting up part widths with bone, position, and direction parameters. Now I'm importing the builder utilities and planning a custom hull paint that blends a dark blue-grey base with warmer highlights near the top, muddy grime toward the bottom, and orange scuff marks using noise-based blending.

Writing the hull paint function...

Defining more material presets...

Setting up the builder scaffold and a box helper function for constructing chassis parts...

Still building wheel and tread geometry...

Now I'm working out the wheel placement loop with joints positioned per side and index, then detailing the tire sidewall and rim as nested cylinders. I'm also checking whether a hull bottom skid plate would overlap with the rail geometry given their vertical positions.

Rather than add a skid plate that conflicts with the rails, I'll keep the rails visible and instead position fuel tanks as cylinders along each side, carefully checking their overlap against the rail edges and tire clearances to make sure everything fits without clipping.

I'm adding strap rings around the tanks and a driveshaft rod running from the cab underside to the rear, keeping clear of the rails. For the front, I'm sketching a simple bull-bar skeleton with upright boxes and a crossbar positioned ahead of the headlights and cab front.

Now I'm sketching the connecting struts linking the bull bar to the hood, adding an amber glow to the roof light bar, then writing the final part code including the windshield box geometry with its tilt rotation.

Positioning the slanted pillar boxes alongside the header frame...

I'll make the window glass dark "#0d2b3a" and skip the reflection strip. For the cab, I'm planning roof armor plates, a visor, light bar, and vents, plus a turret cupola with a dome, a glowing red camera sensor lens, and smoke launcher tubes on each side.

For the turret I'm leaning the smoke launcher tubes outward by rotating them around the z-axis, adding a rear bustle box for ammo storage, ERA tiles merged onto the turret flanks, and a rear antenna with a glowing tip plus a cab sensor eye.

Now I'm placing amber clearance lights on the cab roof corners and planning a radar dish built with a lathe operation, making sure the outline points don't self-intersect before assembling the full vehicle.

Finishing up with a feed rod, tilted dish axis, and a mast cylinder, keeping part count around 220 while confirming the rod signature and SVG text styling before the final write-up.

Now I'm detailing antenna tip spheres with glow, a lathed turret ring with a specific outline profile, and double-checking that shared-material parts still render glow correctly when textures are present. I'm also flagging a potential aspect ratio mismatch on the bumper texture, which could stretch slightly since the plane dimensions don't perfectly match the texture's 4:1 ratio.
